question: Increasing the ability of citizens to use active and public transport modes is crucial for tackling transport-related emissions and improving quality of life. Young people and the elderly often require extra support to be able to make full use of public transport systems, particularly as they have been hit hard by the cost of living crisis. 1.

Does the Commission have data on the availability of extra support measures, such as subsidies or discounted fares, in each Member State for young people and the elderly for accessing public transport?
Does the Commission collect data on the use of public transport systems by these groups of people in society (young people and the elderly)?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (23.4.2024) 1. The Commission does not have data on the measures employed by the Member States to support the use of public transport by different age groups. Some general information on discounted fees in Member States has been collected in the context of a 2022 ‘Study on the social dimension of the future EU transport system regarding users and passengers’1. 2.

Currently, at EU level there is no regular and harmonised data collection that would allow comparable indicators on the use of public transport by age groups. To respond to an increasing need for monitoring mobility, Eurostat developed harmonised guidelines on passenger mobility statistics and offered grants to countries to collect data using this methodology.
The results for the participating countries are published on Eurostat website2, however no breakdown by age group is available.

In addition, the EU-SILC (EU Statistics on Income and Living Conditions) survey will collect every six years from 2024 data on frequency of use of public transport; financial burden of public transport; main reason for not using regularly public transport which will be analysed by age groups (2024 data available in September 2025).

In order to obtain comparable indicators, in 2019 the Commission launched a one-off, comprehensive EU-wide survey on passenger mobility. The survey was carried in 2021 in all Member States and targeted individuals aged between 15-84 years.

The main passenger mobility indicators such as number of trips by travel mode or by travel purpose, travel distance by fuel type, reasons for choosing the car and use of emerging mobility forms are available for different breakdowns, including the age groups: 15-29, 30-64 and 65-843.
